study_name.evidence_quote: The gut microbiota contributes to the pathogenesis of anorexia nervosa in humans and mice
study_name.notes: Study name derived from title and publication year; no explicit study name provided in paper.

target_condition.evidence_quote: The gut microbiota contributes to the pathogenesis of anorexia nervosa in humans and mice

country.evidence_quote: only included Danish Caucasian women with AN cases, recruited from three specialized centres in Denmark

body_site.evidence_quote: Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics were performed on faecal and serum samples
body_site.notes: Primary microbiome samples were faecal (feces); serum samples were also collected but analysed for metabolomics, not 16S/shotgun sequencing at primary level.

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: Microbial DNAs were isolated and purified from stool samples using NucleoSpin soil mini kit
dna_extraction_kit.section: Methods — DNA extraction, 16S rRNA sequencing and data analyses in mice experiments
dna_extraction_kit.notes: Note: This description refers to the mouse experiment DNA extraction. For human samples, paper states 'DNA extraction from aliquots of faecal samples was performed following IHMS SOP P7 V2' without specifying kit name.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: Purified and amplified DNA fragment libraries were sequenced using the Ion Proton Sequencer
sequencing_platform.notes: Human samples were sequenced on Ion Proton. Mouse samples used Illumina MiSeq for 16S rRNA.

sex.evidence_quote: 77 female AN cases and 70 healthy females
sex.notes: Study enrolled only females; 'About 95% of cases are women' and study 'decided to include only women'.

ancestry.notes: Ancestry inferred from 'Danish Caucasian'; Caucasian typically refers to European ancestry.

ancestry_details.evidence_quote: only included Danish Caucasian women with AN cases

westernized.evidence_quote: The control participants were recruited via public advertisement and via direct contact to health staff, medical students and their relatives.
westernized.notes: Inferred as westernized based on Danish/Caucasian population and recruitment from urban healthcare settings; explicitly stated as limitation 'use of a cross-sectional Danish AN cohort limits generalizability'.

zigosity.notes: Twin zygosity not discussed in this microbiome study.

age_min.evidence_quote: EDI-3 was designed for use in females aged 13–53 years.
age_min.notes: EDI-3 age range provided; human participants were adult women from specialized treatment centres.

age_max.evidence_quote: EDI-3 was designed for use in females aged 13–53 years.
age_max.notes: EDI-3 age range provided; specific age distribution of study participants not reported.

age_years.notes: Individual participant ages not reported; only mouse donor ages mentioned (20, 22, 20 and 20, 22, 21 years).

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Exclusion criterion for AN cases; control exclusion also included antibiotics within last 3 months.

bmi.notes: Mean BMI values reported for groups (Supplementary Table 1 and 2 referenced) but not provided in extracted text; individual participant BMIs not listed.

dietary_restriction.notes: Paper notes lack of diet and physical activity information as a limitation; no dietary restriction data extracted.

disease.evidence_quote: AN patients were all diagnosed by an experienced consultant psychiatrist and they met the DSM-5 criteria
disease.notes: Study focuses on Anorexia Nervosa (AN); healthy controls listed separately as disease-free.

disease_details.evidence_quote: the restricting (AN-RS) type and the less prevalent binge-eating or purging (AN-BP) type
disease_details.notes: Two AN subtypes analyzed; study enrolled both restricting and binge/purging subtypes.

disease_response_orr.notes: Overall response rate not applicable; study is mechanistic/observational, not a treatment trial.

disease_response_pfs.notes: Progression-free survival not applicable to eating disorder pathogenesis study.

disease_response_pfs_month.notes: Progression-free survival not measured in this study.

disease_response_recist.notes: RECIST criteria not applicable; not an oncology study.

feces_phenotype.evidence_quote: the AN gut microbiota is characterized by higher β-diversity; Gut microbiota composition is altered in AN
feces_phenotype.section: Results — Gut microbiota composition is altered in AN
feces_phenotype.notes: Multiple stool phenotypes measured including bacterial composition, viral composition, species diversity.

fmt_id.evidence_quote: three randomly chosen AN-RS cases and three age-matched HC participants to three independent litters of female germ-free mice
fmt_id.section: Results — Gut microbiota induces reduced weight gain
fmt_id.notes: Study-specific identifiers inferred from text description; 3 AN donors (ages 20, 22, 20 yr; BMI 10.3, 11.5, 11.7) and 3 HC donors (ages 20, 22, 21 yr; BMI 22.6, 21.1, 21.2) transplanted to GF mice.

fmt_role.notes: FMT roles (donor/recipient) are implicit in the study design but not explicitly labeled per individual participant.

hla.notes: HLA typing not performed in this microbiome study.

value: AN cases: 77 females, age range 20-22 years (mouse model donors), Danish Caucasian ethnicity
Healthy controls: 70 females, age-matched to AN cases
AN diagnostic criteria: DSM-5 criteria for restricting or binge/purging subtypes
Exclusion criteria for AN: antibiotic/antifungal treatment within 3 months, acute/chronic somatic diseases
Exclusion criteria for HC: BMI <18.5 or >25 kg/m², regular medication except birth control, antibiotics within 3 months
Sequencing method: shotgun metagenomics on fecal samples; 16S rRNA for mouse experiments
Metabolomics: untargeted serum profiling (polar and semipolar metabolites, bile acids)
Mouse FMT: germ-free Swiss Webster female mice, 30% energy-restricted diet for 3 weeks
Mouse study duration: 21 days with body weight measurements every 5 days
Recruitment sites: three Danish specialized eating disorder centers
EDI-3 questionnaire used for assessment of eating behavior and psychological traits
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females; shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics on fecal and serum samples; germ-free mice received 30% calorie restricted diet for 3 weeks
uncurated_metadata.section: Methods — Study participants; Results section headers; Animal experiments
uncurated_metadata.notes: Comprehensive methodological and cohort information extracted from Methods section and supplementary tables.

host_species.evidence_quote: 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females; Female germ-free Swiss Webster mice
host_species.section: Abstract; Methods — Study participants; Methods — Animal experiments
host_species.notes: Study involved both human participants (Homo sapiens) and mouse model (Mus musculus). Humans were the primary focus with mechanistic validation in mice.

extraction_warnings: Schema requests 'subject_id' and 'sample_id' as required fields, but the paper does not provide explicit participant IDs or sample identifiers. Entries are inferred/representative.
Paper granularity is study-level (aggregate statistics for 77 AN cases and 70 HC controls). No per-sample metadata table was provided; sample_level entry is illustrative only.

Age values are reported as ranges or group statistics (e.g., 'women', no specific ages given in main text; mice donors aged 20-22 years; mouse recipients 6 weeks old) but not as individual sample-level data.
NCBI accession numbers not explicitly stated in the provided text; paper lists study protocol at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02217384) but no SRA/ENA accessions.
DNA extraction kit identified from mouse 16S methods (NucleoSpin soil mini kit); human shotgun metagenomics used 'IHMS SOP P7 V2' without explicit kit name.
Mouse experiments used Illumina MiSeq (16S rRNA) but human shotgun metagenomic sequencing used Ion Proton; extracted value reflects human cohort primary sequencing platform.
Batch 1 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
Individual participant BMI, age, and clinical phenotypes not provided in extracted text; Supplementary Tables 1 and 2 referenced but not fully reproduced.
Smoking status and medication use documented as study covariates but not reported per-participant.
FMT human donor and recipient participants not individually labeled with study IDs in the main text.
Mouse recipient numbers vary by litter (8, 6, 6 littermates in three independent experiments).
The paper is primarily a mechanistic/observational study of microbiota in AN; many clinical trial-specific fields (ORR, PFS, RECIST) are not applicable.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
Paper focuses on mechanistic pathogenesis study rather than clinical outcomes; therefore disease_response_os, ecog_performance_status, and tumor measurements not applicable.
Biomarker values are predominantly reported as comparisons (higher/lower in AN vs. HC) or correlation directions rather than absolute numerical values with standard units.
Specific numerical biomarker values scattered throughout paper in text and figures; systematic extraction of all individual measurements not performed due to complexity and diversity of metrics.
Study uses complex multi-omics approach (metagenomics, metabolomics, structural variants) with multiple analytes; full enumeration of all measured features would be extensive.
Mouse model experiments represent mechanistic validation of human findings; results are complementary rather than independent clinical outcomes.
